rationales: Ecology studies relationships between organisms and their environment, not parasites specifically.
Morphology studies the form and structure of organisms.
Genetics studies heredity and variation.
Parasitology is the branch of biology that studies parasites.
Chitin is a major component of fungal cell walls, not plant cell walls.
Cellulose is a major component of plant cell walls.
Cholesterol is a sterol found in animal cell membranes, not a major plant cell-wall component.
Glucose is a simple sugar and is not the main structural component of plant cell walls.
Medicine concerns the prevention and treatment of disease.
Agriculture concerns farming and the cultivation of crops and rearing of animals.
Forestry concerns the management of forests.
Horticulture deals with the art and science of gardening and plant cultivation.
Xylem transports water and dissolved minerals through plants.
Phloem transports sugars and other organic substances, not water as its primary function.
Stomata are pores that regulate gas exchange and water loss, not transport tissues.
Leaves are organs that make food; they are not the tissue that transports water through plants.
Melvin Calvin discovered the dark reactions of photosynthesis; the option misspells his first name as “Malvin.”
Karl Lohmann is not credited with discovering the dark reactions of photosynthesis.
Koshland is not credited with discovering the dark reactions of photosynthesis.
T. Schwann is not credited with discovering the dark reactions of photosynthesis.
An experiment tests a deduction rather than serving as its source.
A deduction or prediction is drawn from a hypothesis.
A theory is a well-supported explanation, not the immediate source of a deduction in the scientific method.
A law summarizes a consistent natural relationship and is not the immediate source of a deduction here.
Tubulin forms microtubules, not microfilaments.
Tropomyosin associates with actin filaments but does not form the main microfilament structure.
Myosin is a motor protein that interacts with actin, not the main material of microfilaments.
Actin is the main protein that forms microfilaments.
Parenchyma is a type of ground tissue.
Vessel elements are components of xylem, not ground tissue.
Tracheids are components of xylem, not ground tissue.
Sieve tubes are components of phloem, not ground tissue.
Meiosis produces gametes and is not the cell division whose errors typically lead to tumors.
Errors in mitosis can cause uncontrolled cell division and tumor formation.
Binary fission is a form of cell division used by prokaryotes, not the process implicated here.
Multiple fission is not the process whose errors typically produce tumors.
Apoptosis is programmed, controlled cell death rather than accidental cell death.
Regeneration is the replacement or regrowth of cells or tissues.
Necrosis is accidental, uncontrolled death of cells and tissues.
Fragmentation is a form of reproduction or body division, not accidental cell death.
Amylase is used in some cloth-washing detergents to break down starch stains.
Amylase is not primarily used in dishwashing products for its enzyme action.
Amylase breaks down starch and is not used for colouring.
Saponification is soap formation from fats and alkali, not a use of amylase.
The light reactions are not conventionally called the S-scheme.
The light reactions are not conventionally called the X-scheme.
The light reactions are not conventionally called the Y-scheme.
The sequence of electron transfers in the light reactions is called the Z-scheme.
Arteries carry blood away from the heart.
Capillaries connect arterioles and venules and allow exchange with tissues.
Arterioles carry blood away from the heart toward capillaries.
Veins carry blood toward the heart.
Viruses are not used as the standard host organisms for producing insulin.
Fungi are not the standard microorganisms used for recombinant insulin production.
Algae are not the standard microorganisms used for recombinant insulin production.
Genetically engineered bacteria, such as E. coli, are used to produce insulin.
Jabir bin Hayan is associated with early chemistry, not authorship of Al-Qanun Fi al-Tib.
Ali Ibne Eisa was a physician but was not the author of Al-Qanun Fi al-Tib.
Bu Ali Sina, also known as Avicenna, wrote Al-Qanun Fi al-Tib.
Abdul Malik Asmai was not the author of Al-Qanun Fi al-Tib.
